I genuinely wish there were a way to downvote on this site. There are inherent limitations for Quest users, primarily because the device cannot handle certain high-complexity avatars. VRChat has already made considerable efforts to be more inclusive toward Quest users through features like imposters and the new SDK materials.

What you’re requesting would likely result in frequent crashes — roughly every 20 minutes or so. If you haven’t heard of it, there used to be an add-on called Bloodborn, which allowed Quest users to bypass these built-in limitations. However, even loading just two or three of those avatars in a single world could crash a Quest 3.

The reality is that Quest headsets simply cannot support higher-quality avatars without significantly reducing overall performance — leading to lower frame rates, lag, and long load times. Quest users already face difficulties joining larger worlds or rendering multiple avatars simultaneously.

**Edit:** A skilled avatar creator knows how to properly optimize their work for Quest compatibility while still maintaining strong visual quality.

these ideas though wouldnt create a large impact, such as the preview mirror so its only temporary/reflection. Settings can be changed to accommodate heavier avatars especially among small groups who want to show off to a couple friends. Expanding limits and toggling said limits on and off is easily done in the settings,  Id like the ability to chose to do so. The options are still available for low impact stuff. 20 minutes till a crash ? still enough to showcase and enjoy  your friends fancy avatar, even just a preview. Overall, the chance to preview or temp see our fancy friends would be greatly appreciated. Bridging this gap leads to lots more fun until we get headsets capable of pc renders.

@{6903d1551f833c417c0dded9|full_name}

vrchat as architected uses compiled shaders in what gets uploaded to the live service.  Shaders and texture formats are different, textures can be decoded, but the shaders need interpretation.

With the mobile shaders that vrchat ships with the SDK, they can just recognize and replace the code on the fly, but for any material using a different shader, like poiyomi when a user locks a material the shader goes through a preprocessor and cuts out certain unused sections, so each version and each combination of options looks different. 

I guess with following emulation technologies I know that showing a quest only avatar on PC is a sufficient challenge that I know VRChat would not bother with, and that showing PC avatars on Android would be way more difficult....

details:
Please add a mirror or preview feature so Quest users can see avatars the same way PC users do — including clothing, materials, lighting, and effects like aging or glow.

Right now, Quest players can’t view or experience full avatar designs because of platform limits. Avatars often appear incomplete, breaking immersion and creative intent.

Alongside this, please increase or match Quest’s upload capabilities with PC — allowing larger file sizes, textures, and materials (within safe performance ranges). Creators want to design unified avatars without having to strip down Quest versions.

Ideas:

• Add a “Visual Mirror Mode” that lets Quest users preview PC-level visuals temporarily (mirrors or toggle in worlds).

• Let creators flag key elements (like outfits, glow, or transitions) for simplified Quest rendering.

• Expand Quest upload limits or offer “High Fidelity Quest Mode” for optimized advanced avatars.

Why it matters:

This would bridge the gap between platforms, support creators, and give Quest users the same sense of identity, immersion, and inclusivity PC players already enjoy.

Note*

Just to clarify — this idea isn’t about forcing Quest to run full PC graphics or break performance limits.

It’s about giving Quest users a temporary visual mirror mode to help them: • See how their outfits and colors actually appear to others.

• Preview materials, lighting, glow, and effects — even in a simplified or simulated way.

• Avoid mismatched looks when switching outfits or customizing avatars.

This would make avatar changes smoother, more creative, and more inclusive. Even a lightweight preview or toggle would massively improve the experience for Quest players and creators alike.
title: Visual Mirror Mode & Equal Upload Options for Quest Users
